steps.content: [Foot of the Mountain]

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: What are you planning to do? The direction you're heading leads to the main mountain path, which is now completely blocked by snow and impassable.
Then we'll take a different route. We've also overlooked a crucial clue. The denunciations.
A red plum denunciation was left at every scene. For those people to be so convinced of the divine martial arts' power, Jichuan must've hidden some information inside them.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Your hypothesis is logically sound. But it's not enough reason to continue our involvement.
It is. If contaminated relics from the farlands can draw people in like moths to flame, who's to say the codex doesn't hold something far worse?

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Current intelligence indicates that Sinners are engaged in combat on the mountain. The snowstorm is intensifying. The risk of ascent is critical. Compared to the "potential threat" you're citing, the projected cost-benefit ratio of this operation is far from favorable...
Wasn't it you who said we "can't afford to let any potential threat slip"? That's why we came all the way to Eastia, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: That principle assumed you'd operate rationally within Eastia's trust framework. Right now, your heart rate, breathing, and decision-making patterns all indicate emotional instability—
You grab Schorl and shove it deep into the snow. Sure enough, unequipped for the extreme cold, it freezes instantly, falling silent.
Xiaofeng listens to your entire argument without uttering a word.
Don't worry. I'm calm. My status here as an outsider is... complicated. A lot of people have their eyes on me. I'll explain later.
She scratches at her ears, her expression unusually troubled.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Tch... She didn't warn me about someone this stubborn.
She?

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Look. Coming down to get you? That was those two manor birdies asking me for a favor. I was in the middle of a decent scrap with that old timer when they came flapping over, saying there was something more fun down here.
...So the escape route by the cliffside plum tree was a lie too.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: She traded two jars of fine liquor for that request. I agreed to keep you safe and get you out 'cause I was planning to leave anyway. I never agreed to drag you back up.
Taking a moment to brush off the snow, you confirm that you're uninjured, then pivot and head the other way. The main path is blocked, so you'll have to find another way up the mountain.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Hey, you still not getting it? She went through all that trouble to get you out. She doesn't want you to go back.
I know.
You press on without a pause, the snow rising past your knees. Xiaofeng watches your figure as it slowly vanishes into the whiteout, then lifts her voice and calls out:

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: Going down's easy! Going up? Avalanches wiped out every path. You're not making it up there alone—
I know.

steps.speaker: Xiaofeng
steps.content: And even if you did, you can't change anything. That girl's power burns through her own life... She doesn't have much time left.

options: That's exactly why I'm going back.

steps.content: There's something I didn't get to tell Schorl. Another reason I have to go back.
The shackles in your palm throb, the connection to the other end clear and unwavering. Through them, you feel Jichuan draining her last reserves of strength, locked in an endless, grueling battle.
She never lied about being frail. If she hadn't pushed herself to wield that strength, maybe she could've lived longer, just as an ordinary person.
She still hasn't told me what drives her to pay that price. For the people, yes. But for herself... what's she really fighting for?
You don't look back. Your silhouette grows smaller and fainter against the vast curtain of snow.
